limits.why: 2026-10-24 Rust CI speed pass (#922, #924), measured on the runs below: job count at its measured 43; runner minutes (374.2) and longest job (19.7) about 10% above; critical path 28.1 with the harness build's cache cold on pull-request refs (about 22 once master has saved it), so 33, which still refuses parity waiting on the Rust job (38 or more); 2026-10-26 (#967, PDF ingest): longest job 25 -> 34. Rust / windows-latest measured 31.4 (median of runs 40209914303 and 40223580054): about 26 before this change (#965's run 40223499916, 26.1, and master push 40218426648, 24.2, had already passed the 19.7 the old limit rested on), plus about 4.6 for the PDF tests: provisioning the pinned PDFium library (1.2), pdfium-render compiled in each daemon override build (+1.7) and the Nextest steps (+0.8). 34 is the measured 31.4 plus about 8% 2026-11-05: startup consolidation keeps both logical parts and schema checks in one shard per OS, reducing the physical-job ceiling from 43 to 41; other limits are unchanged. 2026-11-06: one late hosted Linux-pool planner adds one brief job (0.5 min estimated) before the parity burst. The fallback ceiling stays fully hosted; enabling one measured Linux cli-startup shard removes its hosted allocation. Other limits are unchanged. 2026-11-14 (issue #1519): the report-only frozen judge probes leave the Rust job for a job of their own per OS, because a lost probe runner failed Rust / ubuntu-latest twice on 2026-11-13. Those two jobs run only on ordinary pull requests (scope full == false) and never in a batch, but this budget cannot tell, so they are counted: jobs 42 -> 44 and runner minutes 410 -> 447, exactly their estimated 19 + 18 minutes, which leaves a batch the same headroom as before. Longest job and critical path are unchanged. 2026-11-14 (the Python freeze, maintainer ruling): the live-comparison jobs left CI (frozen judge probes, the cli-live and judges suites and every H5 suite: 15 budgeted jobs), so the limits fall to what remains: jobs 29, runner minutes 291 (the 264.7 budgeted minutes plus about 10%, most of them still the pre-freeze measurements of shards that lost their live passes, so a re-measure lowers them). Longest job and critical path are unchanged.

parity.*: the required Parity gate reads every gated job's result

source-mutants.candidate: weekly only: its jobs (two per shard) start only once the candidate compiles, so a broken build spends no runners on them

stress-report.stress-plan: reports only a loop that was planned

parity-pool.*: Read live runner availability only after every candidate and fixture build has finished; an earlier scope snapshot can be stale before shard dispatch.

ordinary_pr.why: Broad ordinary-PR sample: all 20 golden rows and six report-only frozen groups on both OSes; phase selections match across both runs. Batch commands and prices are unchanged; host caches and inherited master changes vary.

limits.why: 2026-10-24: measured on the runs below, each job only on runs of its current definition (guards runs instead of the four test lanes when scope skips them, so the sum overstates a run); limits about 10% above 2026-11-14 (the Python freeze): test-lite-linux, the whole suite on embedded PostgreSQL, left with the lite tier, so the job limit falls to 7; the other limits are unchanged.

guards.estimate: 2026-11-14: a Rust-only batch or push now also runs the 20 live tests that read rust/ files, with a PostgreSQL service. That step took 12.3 min on two workers on a Windows desktop (1,532 passed, 7 platform skips); about 6 is expected on hosted ubuntu-latest, plus the 1.9 measured for the tree-wide guards and about 0.5 for the service. An ordinary pull request skips the step (about 2.4). Re-measure from the first Rust-only batch's run.
